ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against FINTRAC suspicious-transaction reporting requirements, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian listed entities under Criminal Code s. 83.05, and all Canadian autonomous sanctions adopted under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. Politically exposed persons require enhanced due diligence and senior management approval. Standard risk for a low-risk kitting/assembly entity is not an automatic PEP refusal absent sanctions exposure, ML indicators, or adverse media.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level_note: The CBCA beneficial-ownership register is maintained in the corporate records and is disclosed to FINTRAC, CRA, and law-enforcement authorities upon lawful request; it is not a fully public registry. Quebec's enterprise register is public for ordinary legal-publicity data, but the sensitive beneficial-owner information is subject to restricted access and privacy protections.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (https://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/053.nsf/eng/home for federal corporations); Registraire des entreprises du Québec portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca for provincial Quebec incorporation and name reservation).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Federal corporate names may be in English, French, or bilingual. For Quebec incorporation, the legal name in the registre must comply with the Charter of the French Language; it must be in French unless a recognized trademark exception applies. Transliteration of a non-Latin script name into Latin characters must be accompanied by a supporting explanation and is reviewed by the registre for phonetic distinctiveness.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Lawyer, Avocat, Barrister, Solicitor, Notary, Notaire
Medical, Médecin, Physician, Doctor, Surgery, Chirurgie
Royal, Royale, Her Majesty's, Municipal, Government of Quebec or Québec
Any token suggesting government sponsorship, public office, or regulated self-regulatory profession without prior ministerial or regulatory approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A federal name reservation is valid for 90 days; the incorporation filing must be completed within that window and no extension is available. On a federal name refusal, the applicant may file a written reconsideration with Corporations Canada within 30 days of the refusal, attaching a fresh NUANS search report and legal justification. If the refusal is upheld, judicial review may be brought to the Federal Court under section 246 of the CBCA. In Quebec, an applicant may apply to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec for administrative review within 30 days of the refusal; a further appeal is available to the Tribunal administratif du Québec.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in Quebec may be maintained through a registered agent or a commercial virtual office service for service-of-process and records purposes. However, for a 3PL fulfillment and kitting operation, Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency will expect a physical operating presence in Quebec with staff, inventory, storage equipment, and commercial substance. A virtual-only location is not sufficient to establish the operational reality of a warehouse business or to support claimed deductions and GST/QST input credits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 40% — measurable risk of unannounced on-site verification by Revenu Québec or the CRA for warehouse operations, payroll substantiation, inventory matching, and confirmation that the corporation is engaged in its declared commercial activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les societes par actions), CQLR c S-31.1, particularly ss. 16-23 (incorporation and certificate of incorporation), s. 21 (contents of articles of incorporation), ss. 108-110 (board written resolutions); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (registry duties); Regulation respecting the application of the Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, r. 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), 2050 rue Bleury, Montreal, Quebec H3A 2J5; online filing portal 'Mon Registre' at www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (articles de constitution / statuts de constitution) filed electronically in the REQ prescribed form for a business corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; authorized capital may be nominal (e.g., CAD 1 per issued common share) and shares may be issued without par value; no escrow or bank deposit requirement applies to a non-offering private corporation; consideration may consist of cash, property, or past services.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 2025-01 OF [●] INC., adopted as a written resolution by all directors under section 108(1) of the Quebec Business Corporations Act. RESOLVED: (1) the issuance and allotment of [class] shares to the subscribers named in the subscription list, and the consideration received, are ratified and share certificates authorized; (2) the registered office is fixed at [complete street address], Province of Quebec, adopted as head office and principal repository of the corporate minute book and accounting records; (3) [name] is appointed President, [name] appointed Secretary-Treasurer; and (4) the officers are authorized to open and sign for corporate bank accounts and complete all post-incorporation registrations. SIGNED by all directors, effective [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - NUANS name search and reservation service via Mon Registre.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Commission a NUANS attestation and reserve one preferred and two alternate corporate names. The name must include a distinct element and a legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.'); it must not be prohibited or misleading under QBCA name rules. The REQ issues a name reservation valid for 90 days, during which the incorporation filing must be completed.
required_dossiers: Statement of intended business activities (kitting, packaging, 3PL warehousing)
Identity and residential address of each incorporator and intended director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a revised reservation with a stronger distinctive element within the REQ response window; if the refusal persists, adopt a numeric or matricule-based name or file a written review request with the Registraire under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and corporate counsel; final filing authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the articles of incorporation containing the corporate name, place of the registered office in Quebec, share structure (with or without par value), restrictions on share transfers, number of directors, and the names and addresses of initial directors. Each director executes a written consent to act; the instrument is signed by the incorporators or notarized where paper filing is elected.
required_dossiers: Initial director identification and residential addresses
Statement of registered office municipal address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ annotates the draft, correct the defective clause (e.g., share class wording, registered-office locality, director count), re-execute the amended instrument, and resubmit through Mon Registre; no new name reservation is required unless the name itself was challenged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Duty Payment at the Registraire
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - Mon Registre e-filing portal; counter service at 2050 rue Bleury, Montreal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed articles and directors' consents through the secure Mon Registre portal, answer the required enterprise activities declaration, and pay the CAD 322 incorporation duty plus applicable registry fees by credit card or pre-authorized debit. The REQ records the registration in the Quebec enterprise register upon approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A notice of insufficiency identifying missing schedules or inconsistent data is cured by uploading the required documents in Mon Registre within the stated delay and settling any outstanding duty; repeated deficiencies may be resolved by filing a new incorporation instrument with a refund of the prior duty where applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Enterprise Registry Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the REQ issues the certificate of incorporation (attestation de constitution) carrying the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and creates the public registry file. Legal personality commences from the certificate date; the company should verify the registry data and obtain official extracts for banking and contract counterparties.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office municipal address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Clerical or typographical errors in the certificate or registry file are corrected by filing a rectification application with supporting declaration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; delayed issuance beyond the service window is escalated through the REQ priority processing desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Organizational Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the corporation; minutes and records maintained at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene or adopt by unanimous written consent the first board meeting: adopt by-laws or the QBCA model by-law, ratify share subscriptions, authorize share certificates, confirm the registered office fixed in the articles, appoint officers, approve the corporate minute book and seal, and resolve on the audit appointment or unanimous-shareholder audit waiver.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or unanimous written consent
Share subscription lists and share certificates
Minute book with director and shareholder registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any procedural defect in the first board resolution is cured by a further unanimous board resolution ratifying the prior acts; changes of directors or officers and any registered-office changes disclosed at the meeting must be declared to the REQ within 30 days.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and My Business Account, administers federal corporate income tax and GST/HST registration. Revenu Québec administers Québec corporate income tax, Québec sales tax (QST), and related Québec tax registrations through its online services. The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers commercial import and export reporting through the Canada Border Services Agency Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A corporation must obtain a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN) and applicable program accounts, including an RC0001 GST/HST account and, where relevant, an RM import-export account. Registration is generally completed through CRA Business Registration Online, by telephone, or through applicable incorporation and registration channels. A non-resident corporation may register by filing the prescribed CRA registration information and providing incorporation documents, legal name, registered address, directors, ownership and business-activity information, and authorized-representative details. A corporation carrying on business in Québec or making supplies subject to QST generally registers with Revenu Québec for a Québec identification number and QST account, unless a statutory small-supplier or other exception applies. Importers and exporters must establish the applicable CBSA CARM client account and obtain any required importer/exporter program identifiers. Canada does not issue a standalone EU-style VAT number; the GST/HST account number is generally the relevant indirect-tax identifier and is used with the BN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian corporations are generally taxable entities and do not have a general United States-style check-the-box election to be treated as partnerships or disregarded entities. A corporation may qualify for the small business deduction, associated-corporation allocation, capital-cost allowance elections, scientific research and experimental development incentives, and other statutory tax elections, subject to eligibility and prescribed filings. Certain qualifying Canadian-resident corporations may elect under specific provisions to alter the treatment of transactions, reorganizations, amalgamations, wind-ups, or foreign-affiliate arrangements. Canada has anti-hybrid mismatch rules, including restrictions on deductions and foreign tax-credit or dividend treatment for specified hybrid mismatch arrangements; these rules are not an elective entity-classification regime. A Canadian corporation generally remains subject to entity-level taxation even where it has non-resident shareholders.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) federally, together with Québec Sales Tax (QST) in Québec. A Québec fulfillment, kitting, packaging, warehousing, or related logistics business generally analyzes GST/HST and QST separately under federal and Québec place-of-supply, registration, zero-rating, input-tax-credit, and input-tax-refund rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000. For GST/HST, a person is generally a small supplier if taxable supplies do not exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters, subject to sector-specific rules. Québec generally uses a CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold for QST purposes, subject to statutory rules and exceptions. The Québec standard combined consumer rate is 14.975%, comprising 5.000% GST and 9.975% QST. Registration may be required earlier or independently for non-residents, specified supplies, taxable real-property or admissions activities, platform-based supplies, or other prescribed circumstances. A corporation that voluntarily registers may be required to collect tax and may claim eligible input tax credits or input tax refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Québec do not generally impose a nationwide real-time electronic-invoice clearance or mandatory digital-stamping system for ordinary B2B fulfillment, kitting, packaging, warehousing, or logistics invoices. Tax invoices must contain prescribed information when required to support GST/HST input tax credits or QST input tax refunds, including supplier identity and registration number, invoice date, recipient information where applicable, consideration, tax rate, and tax amount. Electronic records are generally acceptable if integrity, accessibility, retention, and audit requirements are satisfied. GST/HST and QST returns are filed through CRA and Revenu Québec portals, and certain registrants may be required to file electronically. Import and export declarations are submitted through CBSA systems, including CARM where applicable. Québec-specific mandatory e-invoicing requirements may apply to particular public-sector or government-procurement arrangements, but no general private-sector real-time clearance requirement applies to this business model.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For GST/HST, goods supplied in Canada and exported from Canada may generally be zero-rated where the statutory export conditions are satisfied, including delivery or transfer of possession outside Canada or shipment by the supplier to a destination outside Canada, depending on the applicable rule. Goods supplied to a non-resident for export may qualify only if the specific regulatory conditions are met, including documentary evidence and restrictions on use in Canada. Services supplied to non-residents may be zero-rated only where they satisfy the statutory exported-service rules; services relating to tangible personal property situated in Canada, real property in Canada, or activities performed in Canada may remain taxable, subject to specific exceptions. For QST, exports of movable property and qualifying services may be zero-rated where the Québec statutory place-of-supply and export conditions are met. A fulfillment or kitting provider must distinguish its own taxable logistics service from the sale or export of customer-owned goods. Input tax credits for GST/HST and input tax refunds for QST generally require valid supporting documentation, commercial-use nexus, and prescribed records. Zero-rating can be denied where goods are consumed, used, or retained in Canada, where the recipient is not eligible, or where export evidence is incomplete.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export declaration or applicable electronic export reporting record, including the required export reporting reference where reporting is mandatory
Commercial invoice or equivalent sales and shipment documentation identifying the exporter, consignee, description, quantity, value, destination, and contractual terms
Bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, or other carrier document evidencing shipment outside Canada
Packing list and warehouse or fulfillment records linking the exported goods to the relevant customer order
Proof of delivery or carrier confirmation showing receipt or delivery outside Canada
Customer purchase order, contract, sales agreement, or written export instructions establishing the commercial purpose and destination
Import entry, customs clearance, or equivalent destination-country evidence where reasonably available
GST/HST and QST tax invoices or credit notes, as applicable, showing zero tax and the statutory basis or transaction description
Payment records, bank statements, merchant settlement reports, or other commercial evidence supporting the transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not generally a Canadian statutory document
Inventory, serial-number, lot, and goods-movement records demonstrating that the goods were not used or consumed in Canada before export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general foreign-exchange-control rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days, and no general statutory inward-remittance certificate is required solely to substantiate GST/HST or QST zero-rating. Tax authorities may nevertheless request contracts, customs records, carrier evidence, proof of destination, inventory records, customer identity, payment evidence, and operational records. If zero-rating is unsupported or incorrectly claimed, the supplier may be assessed the applicable GST/HST or QST, related interest, and penalties, and may lose associated input tax credits or input tax refunds. CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess prior reporting periods within statutory reassessment periods and may extend or reopen periods in cases involving misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, willful blindness, fraud, or other statutory exceptions. GST/HST and QST penalties can apply for false statements, gross negligence, failure to file, failure to remit, failure to maintain records, or failure to provide information. Deliberate tax evasion or fraudulent documentation may trigger civil fraud penalties, prosecution, fines, and imprisonment under applicable federal or Québec law. Customs non-compliance may result in administrative monetary penalties, seizure, accounting adjustments, reassessment of duties and taxes, and enforcement action by CBSA.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); primary federal bank regulator is the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); the Department of Finance Canada has policy authority over the currency; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange control agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current- and capital-account convertibility under the Currency Act and Bank of Canada Act. Canada has not invoked foreign-exchange controls since the 1950s; the Canadian dollar floats freely and there is no central-bank approval requirement for capital movements. Equity subscription, shareholder loans, dividends, royalties, intercompany trade payments, and repatriation of proceeds are all unrestricted. Profit remittance from a Quebec corporation is subject only to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (25% statutory, reduced to 5%-15% by tax treaties) and to solvency tests under the Business Corporations Act (Quebec) or the Canada Business Corporations Act; no exchange clearance or central-bank permit is required. The Investment Canada Act may apply only to large acquisitions or control-of-business reviews, which are not engaged by the creation of a small kitting-and-fulfilment subsidiary.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation for export or collection receipts. An ISIC 5210 cross-border kitting/fulfilment entity may denominate invoices freely in CAD, USD, EUR, or other currencies and may retain foreign currency indefinitely in domestic or foreign-currency bank accounts. The Bank of Canada does not require conversion, and exporters are not obligated to repatriate funds within any period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (CAD/USD)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility, with material legal constraints. Deposit-taking in Canada is a regulated activity reserved for banks licensed under the Bank Act (Schedules I/II/III), federal trust and loan companies, and provincial credit unions. Offshore digital EMIs, including Airwallex, Wise, and Payoneer, may lawfully operate only as FINTRAC-registered money-services businesses (MSBs); they may facilitate cross-border payment collection, FX conversion, and vendor disbursements but cannot serve as the primary Capital Escrow Account because funds held with an unlicensed EMI are not bank deposits, are not CDIC-insured, and are held in pooled omnibus accounts at chartered banks. Recommended treasury architecture: maintain a Schedule I bank account as the legal head treasury and escrow account, and deploy Airwallex solely as a payment-facilitation rail for low-cost cross-border settlements with explicit reconciliation controls.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec incorporated non-resident-owned entity, most Schedule I banks will require at least one signing officer or director to complete an in-person or bank-approved video KYC interview. Physical branch attendance is frequently waived when the applicant is introduced by a reputable foreign correspondent bank or when the signatory's identity is verified through a notarized passport, a certified foreign corporate register extract, and a Canadian legal opinion. Remote opening is permitted on a discretionary basis with enhanced due diligence. Under the Business Corporations Act (Quebec), a majority of directors must be resident Canadians (under the CBCA, at least 25% or one director); a foreign-dominated board must appoint a qualifying resident Canadian director, who will be required for the KYC call. All corporate and KYC documentation must be provided in French or in a bilingual format in accordance with the Charter of the French Language (R.S.Q. c. C-11).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is a non-resident individual or corporate chain lacking a verifiable Canadian nexus; or the UBO is resident in a FATF grey-listed or high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passport and proof of residential address; certified corporate registry extract evidencing the full ownership chain; bank reference letters from the UBO's primary banking institution; audited or accountant-certified source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement; organizational chart certified by counsel; confirmation of non-PEP status; and a written commercial rationale letter describing the kitting, fulfilment, and 3PL operating model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated Quebec subsidiary with minimal share capital and expected high-volume inbound wire transfers disproportionate to the equity base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolution authorizing the capital injection; executed subscription agreement; board minutes; pro-forma 12-month cash-flow model; signed client warehousing and kitting contracts with corresponding invoices; and an explanation of the payment flow between the US parent, Quebec entity, and overseas subcontractors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-compliance with Quebec/CBCA director residency rules (foreign-controlled board without a resident Canadian director).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of appointment of a resident Canadian director, including the executed consent to act, declaration of residency, corporate resolution, and updated letters patent or articles of amendment; or a legal opinion confirming an applicable CBCA exemption and the client's status under Canadian corporate law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade payments involving counterparties in jurisdictions with weak AML regimes (e.g., freight forwarders, packaging subcontractors, or port agents in high-risk locations).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed counterparty KYC pack with beneficial-ownership declaration; executed commercial contracts with defined payment terms; enhanced due diligence questionnaire; transport documentation (bills of lading, packing lists, customs entries); commercial invoices; and evidence of the physical movement of goods consistent with the fulfilment/kitting business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the equity injection as a SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for bank-to-bank) into the Canadian Capital Escrow Account with the beneficiary account listed on the Lynx/RTGS rail. Payment details must reference the shareholder resolution and state 'Equity subscription / authorized share capital' to avoid mischaracterization as taxable consideration. The bank will require a board resolution, a direction letter, a source-of-funds declaration, and the executed subscription agreement. For incoming USD wires, explicitly instruct the receiving bank to settle without auto-conversion to preserve the USD balance; for CAD conversion, apply a separately negotiated spot rate. US-sourced transfers initiated as cross-border ACH will clear at a less favorable rate and are acceptable only for operational cash, not for capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and contractor payments: SWIFT MT103 wire instructions for global non-CAD disbursements; Canadian-dollar transactions clear via Payments Canada Lynx (large-value real-time gross settlement) or ACSS (retail batch for lower-value payments); USD disbursements settle through U.S. correspondent banks such as BMO Harris, RBC/US, or TD Bank, N.A., via Fedwire or CHIPS, or via Cross-Border ACH for recurring small payments. For high-value kitting subcontracts, use an irrevocable confirmed commercial letter of credit (documentary credit) or standby letters of credit for performance guarantees. Real-Time Rail (RTR), Canada's modern real-time payment system, is permissible for immediate low-value CAD disbursements but should not replace MT103 for auditable cross-border trade settlement. Each outbound instruction must carry the relevant invoice and purchase-order references to support transfer-pricing and customs documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot contracts (deliverable, CAD/USD and other freely convertible pairs)
Outright deliverable FX forward contracts (FXA) with tenors up to 24 months
European-style vanilla FX options (call and put structures)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS/XCS) for CAD/USD funding alignment on capital injections

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), permitted only where a non-resident counterparty cannot execute a deliverable CAD contract; not standard for onshore Canadian hedging because the CAD is fully convertible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar, REQ)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the corporation's registration date with REQ
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Corporate fines CAD 1,000–20,000; officer/director fines CAD 1,000–2,000; administrative strike-off by REQ after 7 consecutive years of non-filing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Quebec private non-reporting corporations are exempt from an independent audit only by unanimous shareholder resolution; no statutory revenue or asset threshold. Audit is compulsory for reporting (public) issuers and if any shareholder who is entitled to vote declines the waiver.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public/reporting enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private corporations unless IRFS is voluntarily adopted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The REQ annual declaration must confirm all individuals holding mandatory significant control (25% or more of voting shares or influence) and the updated list of directors. Any share transfer or control change must be filed with REQ within 30 days of the event, and the annual declaration is the annual confirmation checkpoint.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200–800 (CAD 275–1,100) for commercial registered office or local agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–15,000 for a full independent audit; USD 1,500–5,000 for compilation/review if audit waived by shareholder resolution

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined statutory (federal Part I 15.0% + Quebec Part IV 11.5%; M&P preference not applicable to NAICS 493110)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CCPC Small Business Deduction: combined 12.2% (federal 9.0% + Quebec 3.2%) on the first C$500,000 of active business income with phase-out between C$10M and C$15M of taxable capital; refundable SR&ED investment tax credits (federal 35% on first C$3M of qualified expenditures for qualifying CCPCs, Quebec 30%) for qualifying packaging-engineering innovation; no sectoral tax holiday applies to fulfilment/kitting services.
